claims.explanation: logic/experiments.md E03 and src/kernel/tao_correct_solution.py:174-200 describe the staged parity and value scans. C01 is an algebraic decomposition/correctness assertion over valid inputs and associative operators, not a measured scalar comparison. The reported-cell relations do not prove functional equality over all inputs; a finite generated performance experiment would not preserve the asserted algorithmic identity.

src/kernel/tao_correct_solution.py:194-200 uses the shifted positive_count parity and assigns prefix_sum[1:], while logic/experiments.md E01-E02 discusses correctness failures. C02 asserts the necessity of exclusive rather than inclusive prefix counts and wrong output whenever an input element is positive. No installed relation encodes this universal input-dependent semantic assertion; comparing reported runtimes would not test parity correctness.

evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:5-8 gives naive PyTorch time 4.76 ms and reference time 1.6 ms; those cells support a simple ordering. C03 additionally asserts five or more kernel launches with intermediate allocations, an approximately 4-5 ms attained range at N=10^8 and a significant performance difference. No launch-count/allocation table or uncertainty is reported, and the catalog does not express that complete mechanism/range conjunction. Missing variance was not treated as zero.

logic/experiments.md E04:49-59 explicitly says the torch.compile plus CUDA-graph alternative was not scored, and the inference of inferiority comes from file naming and absence of a submission log. evidence/tables/reference_scores.md has only naive PyTorch and official reference rows, not this compiled graph variant. Thus neither the required non-fusion assertion nor its no-sub-reference-performance conjunct has usable matched numeric evidence; a different MALT compiled variant was not substituted.

evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:8 reports the reference target 0.47 and 1.6 ms, while logic/experiments.md E03 and src/kernel/tao_correct_solution.py:153-182 identify the three-kernel pipeline and grid size. There is no independently measured pipeline row separate from the reference anchor. The claim and falsifier require that named configuration achieve score <=0.47 at N=10^8; the catalog lacks a reported absolute-threshold relation. Self-comparing the reference row or checking only speedup over naive PyTorch would be vacuous or weaker.

src/kernel/tao_correct_solution.py:130-143,206-215 shows three warmup calls, graph capture and graph replay. The assertion is that this execution ordering removes JIT compilation from measured calls. No before/after compilation-time or direct-launch versus graph-replay timing table supports the performance falsifier. A numeric relation cannot establish the control-flow mechanism from these source statements alone.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md includes run 343935 attempt 1 and run 343936 attempts 1-2 with textual shape_dtype_match failures and cast recovery; logic/experiments.md E07 summarizes 18 runs. C07 is a dtype-promotion/scorer-contract assertion for all int32-input submissions, including exact acceptance semantics and required repair choices. Numeric score/time relations do not evaluate tensor dtypes or logical scorer fields; null invalid scores were not converted to numeric failures.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md records run 345741 attempt 1 (index 67084935), 345745 attempt 8 (67091334), 345786 attempt 5 (37280717), 345787 attempt 7 (37284089), and 347483 v17 (67134331) in textual invalid-status descriptions. The complete claim asserts a universal float32 precision mechanism past 2^24, a 1-ULP output mismatch and safety of int64 intermediates. The parser provides scores/times, not paired per-element outputs or cumulative magnitudes, and the catalog cannot express this universal precision/correctness conjunction.

logic/experiments.md E05-E06 and evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md describe eager and compiled variants, but C09 requires the two-pass 1.6-GB traffic calculation, attained latency ranges, every observed MALT run above the reference and the necessity of Triton fusion. These are not equivalent to selected runtime comparisons. The table has no measured HBM traffic; several rows (for example run 345786) carry time magnitudes inconsistent with the ms header, and the cited run 347447 attempt 3 is absent. No unit rescaling, cohort filtering or causal claim weakening was applied.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md has wrong-output/null-score single-program attempts (344673, 345742 attempt 3, 345745 attempts 16/18) and valid but slow serial attempts (347450 attempts 1,5-9). C10 is a disjunction of all-zero incorrectness or 1-94-second runtime, universally extended to any grid=(1,) full-array kernel, together with a programming-model explanation. Reported scalar comparisons cannot express the correctness/runtime disjunction or universal kernel-class assertion; null correctness outcomes were not treated as timings.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md identifies block-carry failures in 345743 attempts 3/6, 347447 attempt 11, 347450 attempt 4 and 347483 v6, while logic/experiments.md E10 explains the proposed cause. C11 asserts necessity and insufficiency of specific parity-carry representations and characterizes correct algorithms over arbitrary inputs. The observations are textual correctness statuses, not a relation over reported numeric cells. A finite timing comparison would not preserve this algorithmic correctness claim.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md records 345741 attempts 7/14 as 216.946/233.936-ms compile-dominated runs, 347448 attempts 7/11/13/18-21 as compiled rescoring, and 347450 attempt 16 as a 2.78-ms compiled result. C12 jointly asserts specific eager/compiled magnitudes, reduce-overhead regression, first-call overhead 200 ms-3 s, same-code dispersion of 1.5x-2x, a minority-below-reference count and an autotune cause. The table lacks separate first-call overhead and paired code identities, and omits cited run 347447 attempt 3. No catalog conjunction preserves all those conditions; score-order-only checks would be incomplete.
